comparison: Both evaluate claims C26-C34 regarding stress-induced enhancement of mGluR/IP3 signaling. OpenEval and peer reviewers agree these findings are well-supported. Peer reviewer described the study as 'excellent' and noted careful characterization. Both accepted the dose-dependent and time-dependent effects without challenge.
OpenEval R2 addresses temporal persistence (C35-C36) which peer R1 also covers. Both find these claims supported, with peer reviewers accepting the time-course data without challenge.

Both address IP3 dose-response data (C37-C40). OpenEval finds the leftward shift in EC50 well-supported by appropriate experimental design. Peer reviewers accepted these findings without challenge as part of the mechanistic characterization.

Both evaluate PKA-dependent mechanism (C41-C48). OpenEval finds strong support with appropriate controls. Peer R2 explicitly accepted that authors 'show that PKA-dependent sensitization of IP3-mediated calcium release is a key component,' agreeing on the mechanistic evidence.

Both address LTP enhancement and its relationship to IP3R sensitization (C49-C55). OpenEval finds strong support for the correlation and causal relationship. Peer reviewers accepted the LTP enhancement data itself but extensively critiqued the interpretation of how LTP relates to behavior (addressed separately in peer R10).

Both address C83 regarding IP3R sensitization as the mechanism for LTP enhancement. OpenEval finds this well-supported by correlation and rescue experiments. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted this mechanistic conclusion as part of accepting the LTP enhancement findings.

Both evaluate claims that NMDAR expression/function is unchanged (C56-C58, C117). OpenEval views this as important negative control strengthening IP3R-specific conclusions. Peer reviewers accepted this, with reviewer #2 noting enhancement occurred 'without changing intrinsic firing properties.'

Both address lack of changes in intrinsic excitability (C59-C62, C60-C61, C118). OpenEval finds these negative controls clear and appropriate. Peer reviewer #2 raised concerns, noting lack of firing changes 'might imply these were highly resilient rats' and requested behavioral data on stress susceptibility, marking this as UNCERTAIN.

Both evaluate GR-dependence of stress effects (C74, C133-C137, C79). OpenEval finds the loss- and gain-of-function experiments appropriately demonstrate GR is necessary but not sufficient. Peer reviewers accepted these findings, recognizing GR-dependence as important mechanistic component.

Both address differential mechanisms for stress vs. cocaine-induced IP3R sensitization (C138-C142, C81). OpenEval finds this important control showing GR-specificity for stress. Peer reviewers accepted this distinction without challenge.

Both evaluate enhanced learning/CPP findings (C107-C111, C88, C24). OpenEval finds the behavioral data well-supported. Peer reviewers heavily debated interpretation: reviewer #1 raised major concerns about whether CPP measures learning vs. reward enhancement, remaining 'unsatisfied' even after revision, marking this UNCERTAIN.

Both address parallel GR-dependence of LTP and CPP (C112-C113, C94, C25). OpenEval finds this strengthens the proposed causal relationship. Peer reviewers accepted the parallel GR-dependence data but reviewer #1 strongly challenged the causal interpretation, stating 'there is not a single piece of empirical evidence that the observed LTP promotes the Pavlovian associations.'

OpenEval R15 addresses claims C90-C93, C95 citing prior work linking VTA NMDAR plasticity to CPP, noting the relationship remains correlative. Peer R10 addresses C95, C104-C105, C132 and explicitly rejects these interpretational claims as UNSUPPORTED, with reviewer #1 stating the LTP-CPP link is 'too speculative.'

OpenEval R20 addresses C97-C105 on metaplasticity and learning enhancement, finding the interpretation reasonable but somewhat speculative. Peer R10 explicitly rejects C104-C105 as UNSUPPORTED, criticizing claims that LTP 'drives' learning without empirical causal evidence.

OpenEval R12 addresses main conclusions (C23-C25) finding them well-supported by convergence of cellular and behavioral data. Peer R8 addresses C24 among behavioral claims but marks interpretation as UNCERTAIN due to concerns about whether CPP measures learning vs. reward.

OpenEval R12 addresses C25 as part of main conclusions, finding strong support. Peer R9 addresses C25 and accepts the parallel GR-dependence data but challenges the mechanistic interpretation linking LTP to behavior.
OpenEval R13 addresses C84-C87 ruling out LTCC mechanism based on cited literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this alternative mechanism was not discussed by reviewers.

OpenEval R14 addresses C88-C89 placing findings in context of prior literature. Peer R8 includes C88 as part of behavioral claims but focuses on interpretation concerns rather than the literature contextualization.

OpenEval R16 addresses C96 acknowledging inability to distinguish learning rate from reward magnitude, marking as UNCERTAIN. Peer R8 extensively critiques this same limitation, with reviewer #1 arguing 'enhanced CPP acquisition observed in defeated rats may well be caused by an increase in the primary rewarding action of cocaine itself.'
OpenEval R17 addresses C63-C68 contextualizing findings relative to prior literature on Ih changes, noting differences in paradigm and species. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R18 addresses C69-C73 presenting speculative mechanistic hypothesis linking stress-induced bursting to PKA via D2 signaling, marked as UNCERTAIN. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R19 addresses C75-C80 presenting speculative hypothesis for GR mechanism despite insufficiency alone (C79), marked as UNCERTAIN. Peer R6 addresses C79 as part of GR-dependence findings marked as SUPPORTED, but does not evaluate the speculative mechanistic hypothesis.
OpenEval R21 summarizes main findings (C114-C122) as well-supported. Peer R4 addresses C117 (unchanged intrinsic firing) as part of this summary, accepting it as SUPPORTED.
OpenEval R21 includes C118 (unchanged intrinsic firing) in summary of well-supported findings. Peer R5 addresses C118 but marks as UNCERTAIN due to concerns about stress susceptibility phenotypes.
OpenEval R22 addresses C123-C127 on PKA dependence and regional specificity, finding them well-supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval R23 addresses C128-C132 citing prior work on VTA NMDAR plasticity and CPP. Peer R10 addresses C132 as part of interpretational claims rejected as UNSUPPORTED due to lack of causal evidence.
OpenEval R24 addresses C143-C146 on methodological approach for neuron identification, finding it appropriately supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval R25 addresses C1-C10 providing background on stress effects on learning, finding citations appropriate and logic sound. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval R26 addresses C11-C22 providing background on VTA physiology and NMDAR LTP mechanisms, finding them well-supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval R27 addresses C82 as explicitly speculative reasoning about GR-dependence, marked as UNCERTAIN. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval R29 addresses C106 on established knowledge about drug-cue learning in addiction, finding it appropriately frames significance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
